notes: v1.14.575 — LOCAL SYSTEM STATE MOVES TO SYS. FIRST-DOOR Ship A slice A-2b, the re-home half. ⭐ IT LANDS IN A SURFACE THAT ALREADY EXISTS, AND SYS GROWS BY ZERO ROWS. A-2a deferred this because SYS is row-based (.hdr-agg-row) while #cs-health is a Deck card, making the move a RENDERER REWRITE rather than a relocation. The cheapest correct destination turned out to be already built: the ERRORS sheet subtitles itself "CRASH LOG · DIAGNOSTICS", which is exactly the DIAGNOSTICS item INTEL-DOCK section 2 names for SYS. So the six rows render there and the SYS short list is untouched. ⛔ THAT CONSTRAINT WAS NOT OPTIONAL: INTEL-DOCK section 2 rules that "SYS is a short list of rare actions; it does not grow a tool row", and six loose status rows would have broken it on the same day the ruling landed. ⚠ THE SYS ROW IS RENAMED ERRORS -> DIAGNOSTICS, a deliberate one-word addition to the slice. Without it the re-home would be less findable than what it replaced: a technician looking for system state would have had to guess it lives behind a row labelled ERRORS. The name is the one INTEL-DOCK section 2 already assigns, so this builds toward the ruled shape rather than away. ⛔ BOTH RENDER BRANCHES CARRY THE BLOCK, AND THAT IS THE TRAP IN THIS SHIP. rd_renderErrors RETURNS EARLY when the crash log is empty — which is the COMMON case — so appending the rows only to the entries path would have shown local system state exclusively on devices that had already crashed. Same shape as the #cs-build early return checked in A-2a, and much easier to miss. ⭐ EVERY ROW REMAINS A VALUE PHANTOM CAN ANSWER FROM LOCAL STATE. The constraint is inherited verbatim: no power-domain, cooling or network-fabric row, because the app receives no such telemetry, and the on-screen caption still says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. ⛔ THE DESKTOP GRID PLACEMENT GOES WITH THE CARD. #cs-health held column 2 row 2; left in place that rule would have reserved a row in a column with nothing to put in it. Column 2 now holds only the shift door and the hero keeps column 1 — the same container-shaped discipline A-2a established, because the deletion is markup and applies at every width while the placement is desktop-only. NOT IN THIS SHIP: A-3 (#cs-lower: fieldops + fieldtools) and A-4 (the readiness indeterminate gate). INTEL-DOCK itself is sequenced after Ship A completes and is not started.
